title: 4.1–4.3 Catch-Up
contentObjective: I can show I am caught up on Lessons 4.1–4.3 by using each lesson's big idea in mixed practice.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Power-Up Boost
revealWordProblem.text: In the arcade game, your base score is 80 points. A rare power-up boosts your score to 250% of your base. How many points do you have after the power-up? (Hint: 250% means 2.5 times the base.)
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 250% = 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5, so 2.5 × 80 = 200 points. Because 250% is greater than 100%, the new score (200) is more than the base score (80).

vocabulary.definition: A rate compares different units; a unit rate compares a quantity to 1 unit.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa compara unidades diferentes; una tasa unitaria compara una cantidad con 1 unidad.
vocabulary.visual: 180 miles in 3 hours = 60 miles per 1 hour.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares two quantities with different units is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tres maneras equivalentes de nombrar la misma parte de un todo.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares a number to 100, written with a % sign, is a ___.

vocabulary.term: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
vocabulary.termEs: Porcentajes mayores que 100% y menores que 1%
vocabulary.definition: Percents can describe amounts greater than one whole or smaller than one hundredth of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los porcentajes pueden describir cantidades mayores que un entero o menores que una centésima de un entero.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.
vocabulary.cloze: A rate that tells the cost or amount for one unit is a ___.

examples.why: It gives the amount for exactly one unit.
That is a rate for 3 units, not a unit rate.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show parts of a whole is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: A percent bigger than 100%, more than the whole thing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje mayor que 100%, más que todo el entero.
vocabulary.cloze: A percent that represents more than one whole, like 150%, is ___.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 4.1–4.3: 4.1 Rates and Unit Rates, 4.2 Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents, 4.3 Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 4.1–4.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 4.1: To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of items. The lower cost per item is the better buy. • 4.2: To turn a fraction into a percent, build an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100: ask “what do I multiply the denominator by to get 100?” and multiply the numerator by that same number. The new numerator is the percent. • 4.3: To change any percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left).

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 4.1 — Rates and Unit Rates: To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of items. The lower cost per item is the better buy.

Lesson 4.2 — Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents: To turn a fraction into a percent, build an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100: ask “what do I multiply the denominator by to get 100?” and multiply the numerator by that same number. The new numerator is the percent.
Lesson 4.3 — Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%: To change any percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left).

explore.instructions: Sort each value into the correct category: Greater than 100%, Between 1% and 100%, or Less than 1%.

discourse.prompt: What do you notice about the decimal form of percents in each category?
discourse.sentenceFrame: Percents greater than 100% have a decimal value ___ than 1, while percents less than 1% have a decimal value ___.

diagram.title: One whole vs. 400% of it
diagram.caption: The top bar is one whole (100% = 15 points). The bottom bar stacks four of those wholes, so 400% = 60 points — four times the whole, not part of it.

optional.stem: (Lesson 4.1) The Star Blaster cabinet scored 90 points in 3 games. What is the unit rate in points per game?
optional.explanation: Divide points by games: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 points per game.
choiceFeedback: You found 90 × 3 — check: should you multiply or divide to find the rate for one game?
You picked 3 — is that the total points or the points for one game?
You found 90 + 3 — remember, a unit rate comes from dividing, not adding.
optional.stemEs: La máquina Star Blaster marcó 90 puntos en 3 juegos. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad en puntos por juego?
optional.explanationEs: Divide los puntos entre los juegos: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 puntos por juego.
hints: A unit rate tells you the amount for exactly one of something — here, for one game.
Divide the quantity named first (points) by the quantity named second (games).
Set up 90 ÷ 3 and think about how many 3s fit into 90.
hintsEs: Una tasa por unidad indica la cantidad que corresponde a exactamente uno: aquí, a un juego.
Divide la cantidad nombrada primero (puntos) entre la cantidad nombrada después (juegos).
Plantea 90 ÷ 3 y piensa cuántos 3 caben en 90.

optional.stem: (Lesson 4.2) Your arcade scoreboard reads 0.25 of the level cleared. What percent and fraction match this score?
optional.explanation: Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = 25%. As a fraction, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.
choiceFeedback: Remember: multiply the decimal by 100, or move the decimal point right 2 places.
Check your conversion — 0.25 as a percent should be higher.
Not quite. Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = ___%.
optional.stemEs: El marcador de tu arcade indica 0.25 del nivel completado. ¿Qué porcentaje y qué fracción corresponden a este puntaje?
optional.explanationEs: Mueve el punto decimal dos lugares: 0.25 = 25%. Como fracción, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.
hints: A decimal, a percent, and a fraction can all name the same amount — percent simply means “out of 100”.
To turn a decimal into a percent, multiply by 100 (move the decimal point two places right). To turn it into a fraction, read the decimal using place-value words.
0.25 reads as twenty-five hundredths, so start the fraction as 25/100 — then move the decimal two places for the percent and simplify the fraction.
hintsEs: Un decimal, un porcentaje y una fracción pueden nombrar la misma cantidad: porcentaje significa simplemente «de cada 100».
Para convertir un decimal en porcentaje, multiplica por 100 (mueve el punto decimal dos lugares a la derecha). Para convertirlo en fracción, lee el decimal con palabras de valor posicional.
0.25 se lee veinticinco centésimos, así que empieza la fracción como 25/100; después mueve el punto dos lugares para el porcentaje y simplifica la fracción.

optional.stem: (Lesson 4.3) A power-up boosts your damage to 150% of normal. Written as a decimal and a fraction, 150% equals:
optional.explanation: 150% = 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5, and 150/100 simplifies to 3/2. It is more than one whole, so the decimal is greater than 1.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 150% = 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5, and 150/100 simplifies to 3/2.
Convert 150% to a fraction with 100.
You moved the decimal point too many places. 150% is divided by 100, not 1,000, and the result has to be greater than one whole.
optional.stemEs: Una mejora aumenta tu daño a 150% de lo normal. Escrito como decimal y como fracción, 150% es igual a:
optional.explanationEs: 150% = 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5, y 150/100 se simplifica a 3/2. Es más de un entero, así que el decimal es mayor que 1.
hints: Percent means 'out of 100', so 150% means 150 out of 100 — more than one whole.
To get the decimal, divide by 100. To get the fraction, write the percent over 100 and simplify.
Write 150/100, then divide the top and bottom by 50. For the decimal, move the point in 150 two places to the left.
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa «de cada 100», así que 150% son 150 de cada 100: más de un entero.
Para el decimal, divide entre 100. Para la fracción, escribe el porcentaje sobre 100 y simplifica.
Escribe 150/100 y luego divide el numerador y el denominador entre 50. Para el decimal, mueve el punto de 150 dos lugares a la izquierda.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.1) A booth charges $4.50 for 9 games. What is the unit rate?
choiceFeedback: Double-check your division: $4.50 ÷ 9 — is it $0.45 or $0.50?
Divide the cost by the number of games: $4.50 ÷ 9, not some other operation.
That's the total cost for all 9 games, not the cost for one game.
hints: You know the total cost ($4.50) and the total games (9). A unit rate tells the cost of just ONE game.
To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of games so the second quantity becomes 1.
Set up the division: $4.50 ÷ 9. Think of $4.50 as 450 cents if that makes the division easier.
approaching.stemEs: Un puesto cobra $4.50 por 9 juegos. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad?
hintsEs: Conoces el costo total ($4.50) y el total de juegos (9). Una tasa unitaria dice el costo de UN solo juego.
Para hallar una tasa unitaria, divide el costo total entre el número de juegos para que la segunda cantidad sea 1.
Plantea la división: $4.50 ÷ 9. Piensa en $4.50 como 450 centavos si eso te facilita la división.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.1) A car travels 180 miles using 6 gallons of gas. What is the unit rate in miles per gallon?
choiceFeedback: That's the number of gallons — you need to divide 180 by 6, not use 6 as the answer.
That's the total miles — divide 180 by 6 to find miles for one gallon.
Check your division: 180 ÷ 6 — is it 30 or 36?
hints: Notice the units in the question: miles PER gallon. That tells you miles go on top and gallons on the bottom.
Divide the total miles by the total gallons so you get the miles for just 1 gallon.
Start the division: 180 ÷ 6. Think: 6 × what number lands on 180?
approaching.stemEs: Un carro recorre 180 millas usando 6 galones de gasolina. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad en millas por galón?
hintsEs: Fíjate en las unidades de la pregunta: millas POR galón. Eso te dice que las millas van arriba y los galones abajo.
Divide el total de millas entre el total de galones para obtener las millas de 1 solo galón.
Empieza la división: 180 ÷ 6. Piensa: 6 × ¿qué número da 180?

choiceFeedback: Try again: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 as well.
Build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 — multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
hints: Percent means out of 100. What do you multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100?
5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the numerator by that same 20 to build the equivalent fraction.
3 × 20 = 60, so 3/5 = 60/100. A fraction out of 100 IS the percent.
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa de cada 100. ¿Por cuánto multiplicas el denominador 5 para llegar a 100?
5 × 20 = 100, así que multiplica el numerador por ese mismo 20 para formar la fracción equivalente.
3 × 20 = 60, entonces 3/5 = 60/100. Una fracción de cada 100 ES el porcentaje.

choiceFeedback: Double-check: 20 × 5 = 100, so the top must be multiplied by 5 too.
Scale 7/20 up to a denominator of 100 first.
hints: The denominator 20 is friendly: 20 × 5 = 100, and percents are always 'out of 100'.
Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 by multiplying top AND bottom by the same number.
Multiply 7/20 by 5/5: the bottom becomes 100. Whatever the top becomes is your percent.
hintsEs: El denominador 20 es amigable: 20 × 5 = 100, y los porcentajes siempre son 'de cada 100'.
Forma una fracción equivalente con denominador 100 multiplicando arriba Y abajo por el mismo número.
Multiplica 7/20 por 5/5: la parte de abajo se vuelve 100. Lo que quede arriba es tu porcentaje.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.3) Which of the following is greater than 100%?
approaching.explanation: 1.25 = 125%, which is greater than 100%. The other values are all less than 1 (less than 100%).
choiceFeedback: 0.75 is worth 75%, which is less than one whole. To go past 100%, the number has to be greater than 1.
A percent greater than 100% is more than a whole.
99/100 = 99% — just under one whole, so not more than 100%.
hints: 100% equals exactly 1 whole. A value greater than 100% must be greater than 1.
Rewrite each choice as a decimal and ask: is it more than 1?
Test 0.75 first — it is less than 1, so it is under 100%. Check 3/4, 1.25, and 99/100 the same way.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál de los siguientes es mayor que 100%?
approaching.explanationEs: 1.25 = 125%, que es mayor que 100%. Los demás valores son todos menores que 1 (menores que 100%).
hintsEs: 100% es exactamente 1 entero. Un valor mayor que 100% debe ser mayor que 1.
Reescribe cada opción como decimal y pregunta: ¿es más que 1?
Prueba primero 0.75: es menor que 1, así que está por debajo de 100%. Revisa 3/4, 1.25 y 99/100 igual.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.3) What is 200% written as a decimal?
approaching.explanation: 200% ÷ 100 = 2.0. Percents greater than 100% become decimals greater than 1.
choiceFeedback: Divide 200 by 100, or move the decimal point left 2 places.
200% is twice as much, so the decimal should be 2 point something.
That is what you get if you divided by 100 too many times. Instead: 200 ÷ 100 = ___.
hints: 200% is more than 100%, so its decimal must be bigger than 1 — that rules out any tiny decimal.
Percent → decimal: divide by 100 (slide the decimal point two places left).
Start at 200. and hop the decimal two places left: 200 → 20.0 → one more hop lands where?
approaching.explanationEs: 200% ÷ 100 = 2.0. Los porcentajes mayores que 100% se convierten en decimales mayores que 1.
hintsEs: 200% es más que 100%, así que su decimal debe ser mayor que 1: eso descarta cualquier decimal diminuto.
Porcentaje → decimal: divide entre 100 (desliza el punto decimal dos lugares a la izquierda).
Empieza en 200. y salta el punto dos lugares a la izquierda: 200 → 20.0 → ¿dónde cae con un salto más?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.1) Which token pack from the table above is the best deal?
onLevel.explanation: Pack B has a unit rate of $0.20 per token, which is the lowest cost per token.
choiceFeedback: Compare the cost per token, not the total price or the total number of tokens. Divide each pack's price by its tokens and compare those results.
A bigger pack is not automatically cheaper for each token. Work out price ÷ tokens for every pack before deciding.
Compare the unit rates: $0.25, $0.20, and $0.25. Are all three the same?
hints: The 'best deal' is the pack where ONE token costs the least — not the pack with the most tokens.
Line up the three unit rates you found in the table and look for the smallest cost per token.
Compare $0.25, $0.20, and $0.25 per token. Which of those is the smallest amount of money?
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuál paquete de fichas de la tabla de arriba es la mejor oferta?
onLevel.explanationEs: El paquete B tiene una tasa por unidad de $0.20 por ficha, que es el menor costo por ficha.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.1) Runner A completes 4 laps in 12 minutes. Runner B completes 5 laps in 14 minutes. Who runs more laps per minute?
onLevel.explanation: Runner A: 4÷12 ≈ 0.33 laps/min. Runner B: 5÷14 ≈ 0.36 laps/min. Runner B runs slightly more laps per minute.
choiceFeedback: You found 4 ÷ 12, but compare: is 0.33 laps per minute more or less than 0.36?
Divide each runner's laps by their minutes. You should get two different rates.
You have the laps and the minutes for both runners — that's enough to find and compare their rates.
hints: Each runner has laps and minutes. 'More laps per minute' means you need each runner's laps-per-minute rate first.
Divide laps by minutes for BOTH runners, then compare the two decimals — bigger decimal means faster.
Start with Runner A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 laps per minute. Now find Runner B's rate with 5 ÷ 14 and compare.
onLevel.stemEs: El corredor A completa 4 vueltas en 12 minutos. El corredor B completa 5 vueltas en 14 minutos. ¿Quién da más vueltas por minuto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Corredor A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 vueltas/min. Corredor B: 5 ÷ 14 ≈ 0.36 vueltas/min. El corredor B da un poco más de vueltas por minuto.
hintsEs: Cada corredor tiene vueltas y minutos. 'Más vueltas por minuto' significa que primero necesitas la tasa de vueltas por minuto de cada uno.
Divide vueltas entre minutos para AMBOS corredores y luego compara los dos decimales: mayor decimal significa más rápido.
Empieza con el Corredor A: 4 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.33 vueltas por minuto. Ahora halla la tasa del Corredor B con 5 ÷ 14 y compara.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.2) A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
onLevel.explanation: 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number, so divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. That is 87.5 out of 100.
choiceFeedback: 8 will not scale to 100 evenly — divide 7 by 8, then multiply by 100.
Convert the fraction to a decimal first.
Not quite. 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number, so divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = ___.
hints: Try the out-of-100 move first: is there a whole number you can multiply 8 by to get exactly 100?
There isn't (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so use the backup method: divide the numerator by the denominator.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, which is 87.5/100 — slide the decimal two places right to read the percent.
onLevel.stemEs: Un juego muestra tu puntaje como 7/8 completado. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
onLevel.explanationEs: 8 no escala a 100 con un número entero, así que divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, y 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. Eso es 87.5 de cada 100.
hintsEs: Prueba primero el paso de cada 100: ¿hay un número entero por el que puedas multiplicar 8 para llegar exactamente a 100?
No lo hay (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), así que usa el método de respaldo: divide el numerador entre el denominador.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, que es 87.5/100; desliza el punto dos lugares a la derecha para leer el porcentaje.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 4.2) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Divide the bottom by the top

onLevel.correctWork: The student divided in the wrong order. To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the TOP by the bottom: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, then × 100 → 62.5%. So 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (A check: 5/8 is less than 1, so the percent must be under 100%, never 160%.)
hints: Is 5/8 more or less than one whole? Then can its percent be over 100%?
8 will not scale to 100 evenly, so divide the numerator by the denominator: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, which is 62.5/100 → 62.5%.
onLevel.explanation: The fraction bar means numerator ÷ denominator, so this division is upside down. It should be 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, and 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. A quick check catches it: 5/8 is less than one whole, so its percent must be under 100% — 160% was impossible.
onLevel.explanationEs: La barra de fracción significa numerador ÷ denominador, así que esta división está al revés. Debe ser 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, y 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. Una comprobación rápida lo detecta: 5/8 es menor que un entero, así que su por ciento tiene que ser menor que 100%; 160% era imposible.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.3) A player scored 0.4% of the bonus points. Which decimal represents this percent?
onLevel.explanation: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004. Move the decimal point two places to the left.
choiceFeedback: 0.4 is the number in front of the % sign, not the equivalent decimal. You still need to divide by 100.
Move the decimal point left 2 places in 0.4%.
That is what you get if you multiplied by 1000 too many times. Instead: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = ___.
hints: 0.4% is less than 1%, so the matching decimal must be smaller than 0.01.
Divide the percent by 100: the decimal point moves two places left, and zeros fill the gaps.
Start at 0.4 and hop the decimal left twice: 0.4 → 0.04 → one more hop gives the answer's form.
onLevel.stemEs: Un jugador obtuvo 0.4% de los puntos de bonificación. ¿Qué decimal representa este porcentaje?
onLevel.explanationEs: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004. Mueve el punto decimal dos lugares a la izquierda.
hintsEs: 0.4% es menos que 1%, así que el decimal correspondiente debe ser menor que 0.01.
Divide el porcentaje entre 100: el punto decimal se mueve dos lugares a la izquierda y los ceros llenan los huecos.
Empieza en 0.4 y salta el punto dos veces a la izquierda: 0.4 → 0.04 → un salto más da la forma de la respuesta.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 4.3) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A rare item has a 0.8% drop chance. Write 0.8% as a decimal.

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: The student divides 0.8 by 10 instead of 100, moving the decimal only one place.

onLevel.correctWork: To change a percent to a decimal, always divide by 100 — move the decimal point TWO places to the left, not one. 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008. So 0.8% = 0.008, which is far less than 1% (0.01), matching the tiny drop chance in the problem.
hints: Dividing by 100 moves the decimal two places, not one — dividing by 10 is a different operation.
0.08 would actually mean 8%, which is much bigger than the tiny 0.8% drop chance described in the problem.
onLevel.explanation: In the Attempt step the student divided by 10 and moved the decimal only one place. Percent to decimal always means dividing by 100, so 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008 — a value below 0.01, which matches a drop chance smaller than 1%.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso del intento, el estudiante dividió entre 10 y movió el punto decimal solo un lugar. Pasar de porcentaje a decimal siempre significa dividir entre 100, así que 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008, un valor menor que 0.01, que coincide con una probabilidad de aparición menor que 1%.

extending.title: (Lesson 4.1) Find the Rate Error

workedExample.label: Find the unit rate: 12 tickets for $8
Write the unit rate
workedExample.work: The unit rate is $1.50 per ticket

extending.correctWork: To find cost per ticket, divide $8 ÷ 12 = $0.67 per ticket (rounded). The student divided tickets by cost instead of cost by tickets.
hints: What should go in the numerator — the cost or the tickets?
To find 'dollars per ticket,' divide dollars by tickets: $8 ÷ 12 ≈ $0.67 per ticket.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la tasa
extending.explanation: The two quantities were divided in the wrong order. "Dollars per ticket" puts dollars on top, so the correct division is $8 ÷ 12 ≈ $0.67 per ticket. The student's 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 answers a different question, and $1.50 per ticket would mean 12 tickets cost $18 instead of $8.
extending.explanationEs: Las dos cantidades se dividieron en el orden equivocado. "Dólares por boleto" pone los dólares arriba, así que la división correcta es $8 ÷ 12 ≈ $0.67 por boleto. El 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 del estudiante responde otra pregunta, y $1.50 por boleto significaría que 12 boletos cuestan $18 en lugar de $8.

extending.title: (Lesson 4.2) Find the Conversion Error
hints: 2 ÷ 3 doesn't terminate — is 0.67 the exact decimal?
0.67 is rounded. The precise decimal is 0.666... (repeating), making the percent 66.7% or 66⅔%.
extending.explanation: The division is set up the right way, but 2 ÷ 3 does not end — it gives 0.666... repeating. Writing 0.67 rounds the value, so the percent it produces (67%) is rounded too. The exact answer is 66.7% or 66⅔%.
extending.explanationEs: La división está planteada correctamente, pero 2 ÷ 3 no termina: da 0.666... periódico. Escribir 0.67 redondea el valor, así que el por ciento que resulta (67%) también queda redondeado. La respuesta exacta es 66.7% o 66⅔%.

extending.title: (Lesson 4.3) Find the Percent Error

workedExample.label: Move the decimal two places left

extending.correctWork: 0.6% means 0.6 out of 100. Move the decimal two places left: 0.6 → 0.006. The correct answer is 0.6% = 0.006.
hints: The student only moved the decimal one place instead of two.
0.6% is less than 1%, so the decimal must be less than 0.01. 0.06 is too large.
extending.explanation: The step that moves the decimal shifted 0.6 only one place, landing on 0.06 instead of 0.006. Since 0.6% means 0.6 out of 100, the decimal point moves two places left, and the result must be below 0.01 because 0.6% is less than 1%.
extending.explanationEs: El paso que mueve el punto decimal movió 0.6 solo un lugar y llegó a 0.06 en vez de 0.006. Como 0.6% significa 0.6 de cada 100, el punto decimal se mueve dos lugares a la izquierda, y el resultado debe ser menor que 0.01 porque 0.6% es menor que 1%.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1% is treating every percent-to-decimal conversion the same way regardless of size — for example, writing 150% as 0.15 (as if it were an ordinary under-100% percent) instead of 1.5, or writing 0.5% as 0.5 (forgetting to divide by 100 at all) instead of 0.005. Before finalizing an answer, check that the decimal for any percent over 100% is greater than 1, and the decimal for any percent under 1% is less than 0.01.

diagram.title: 300% Jackpot of 30 Tokens
diagram.caption: The top bar is your 30 tokens (100% = one whole); the jackpot bar stacks three 30-token wholes, so 300% = 90 tokens — more than what you put in.

connect.scenario: A different arcade machine pays a jackpot of 300% of your tokens if you win. You inserted 30 tokens. One friend says the jackpot is 90 tokens. Another friend says it's 33 tokens.
connect.promptQuestion: Who is correct, and how many tokens does the jackpot pay?
connect.prompt: The friend who said ___ tokens is correct because 300% of 30 = ___ × 30 = ___. The other friend treated 300% as if it were ___% instead.

check.stem: What is 300% written as a decimal?

check.explanation: 3 × 30 = 90 tokens. The jackpot is three times what you put in.

check.stem: The other friend said 33 tokens. What percent of 30 is 33?
check.explanation: 33 ÷ 30 = 1.1 = 110%. That friend added a small amount instead of tripling — a common slip when a percent is over 100.

connect.modelAnswer: 300% = 3, so 300% of 30 = 3 × 30 = 90 tokens. The friend who said 90 is correct. A percent greater than 100% means MORE than the whole, so the jackpot is three times your 30 tokens. The friend who said 33 was really finding 110% of 30.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 4.2) Which shows 0.45 as a fraction and a percent?
choiceFeedback: Try converting 0.45 to a fraction and percent differently.
Check: 0.45 as a fraction should be 45/100, and as a percent is 45%.
Not quite. 0.45 = 45/100 = ___ (simplified).
hints: 0.45 is 'forty-five hundredths' — that phrase hands you both the fraction AND the percent.
Write 0.45 over 100 as a fraction and simplify; for the percent, multiply the decimal by 100. Check that a choice matches BOTH.
Start with 45/100 and divide top and bottom by 5. Then compute 0.45 × 100 for the percent, and match both parts.

questions.explanation: 0.75 = 75/100. Simplify by dividing both by 25: 75÷25 = 3 and 100÷25 = 4. So 0.75 = 3/4.
